summary: Phase 30 Field Memory backend validation. Parity-lock pytests (10/10) pass against mocked deps. Live integration tests against deployed backend (REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL) found ONE CRITICAL backend bug: the role x subject_kind write matrix is broken for every real portal user. Admin (legacy break-glass token) works correctly; basic CRUD, resolve flow, double-resolve, validation (400s), missing-id 404, append-only doctrine (no DELETE route), and Phase 28/29 regression endpoints all pass.

critical.issue: Role x subject_kind matrix is non-functional for every real portal user. _actor_meta() in /app/backend/routes/field_memory.py (lines 90-96) reads actor.get('role'), but the upstream _require_any_portal_token dependency returns the user's job TITLE in that field (e.g., 'Dispatcher', 'Shop Manager', 'Superintendent'), not the portal kind slug. The actual portal kind is in actor['_actor'] (values: 'admin'|'safety'|'hr'|'shop'|'pm'|'dispatch'|'leadership'|'fl'). Result: Dispatch user gets 403 even for 'assignment', Shop user gets 403 even for 'equipment', Field Leadership user (Superintendent) gets 403 even for 'project'. Only the legacy admin-break-glass token works because that path explicitly hardcodes name='Admin' with no role, causing _actor_meta to fallback to role='admin'. Note: 'fl' must also map to 'field_leadership' in _can_write_subject for FL users to write.

action_items: Fix _actor_meta (and/or _can_write_subject) in /app/backend/routes/field_memory.py to derive the portal-kind role from actor['_actor'] (mapping 'fl' and 'leadership' to 'field_leadership') instead of actor['role'] which is the human-readable job title. Suggested patch: role = (actor.get('_actor') or actor.get('role') or 'admin').lower(); if role in ('fl','leadership'): role = 'field_leadership'.

After fix, re-run /app/backend/tests/test_phase30_field_memory_live.py — the 4 TestRoleMatrix::test_*_can_write_* tests should flip green and captured_by_role should equal the portal kind (dispatch/shop/field_leadership/pm/safety/hr).

Consider also exposing the user's display name from upstream user docs so captured_by stays human-readable (currently legacy admin path stamps 'Admin' which is fine; portal users stamp their .name field — verify those are display names not slugs).
critical_code_review_comments: BUG: role matrix bypassed/broken — see backend_issues.critical above.

MIXED: field_memory.py is clean (≤280 lines, async, Pydantic, append-only doctrine respected). The parity-lock unit tests pass because they MOCK the auth dep with the canonical slug — this is exactly the gap that hid the live-wire bug. Recommend adding ONE live integration test under tests/ (similar to test_phase30_field_memory_live.py) that uses a real per-portal login to lock the actor->role wiring contract.

MINOR: _can_write_subject() recognizes 'field_leadership' but the upstream dep emits '_actor': 'fl' for per-user FL accounts (iter314) and 'leadership' for the shared-password gate. Even after fixing _actor_meta, the matrix must alias both to 'field_leadership'.
GOOD: ensure_field_memory_indexes() is idempotent and wrapped in try/except — startup safe.
GOOD: No DELETE route is registered; verified by both unit test and live integration (DELETE returns 404).

success_rate.backend: 17/23 tests passed = 74% (parity-lock 10/10 + live 7/13 + regression 5/5 with 1 known flake). Critical role-matrix failures are the SAME bug surfacing across 4 tests. Excluding that one bug, effective coverage is 21/23 = 91%.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: /app/backend/routes/field_memory.py::_actor_meta (lines 90-96) maps actor->{name, role} by reading actor['role']. Upstream dependency /app/backend/routes/integrations/_deps.py::make_require_any_portal_token spreads the user doc with _actor=<portal_kind>, so for a real Dispatch user the returned dict is {'role': 'Dispatcher', 'name': 'Dispatcher', ..., '_actor': 'dispatch'}. _actor_meta picks the human-readable 'Dispatcher' as role; _can_write_subject lowercases to 'dispatcher' which is NOT in any allowed bucket → 403 for everyone except the legacy admin break-glass (which is a hardcoded dict with no role key, so role defaults to 'admin'). REPRODUCTION: POST /api/field-memory with X-Dispatch-Token (valid live token) and subject_kind='assignment' returns 403 with body "'Dispatcher' cannot record field memory for 'assignment'" — the literal title leaks into the error string, confirming the bug. MITIGATION: change _actor_meta to read actor.get('_actor') first, mapping 'fl'/'leadership' to 'field_leadership'. One-line fix in field_memory.py.
